metadata.purpose: Real, genuine, thoughtful insights/hacks/strategies for parents planning summer + year-round enrichment for elementary and middle school kids.

sections.title: Registration window cheat sheet — when to actually book

items.label: December–January
items.detail: Member registration opens at top-tier museum/zoo camps in major metros (Pacific Science Center, Woodland Park Zoo, Burke Museum, Seattle Children's Theatre). Premium camps fill in days. If you're not yet a member, the membership pays for itself just from earlier access.

items.label: February (Early Bird windows)
items.detail: Camp Galileo Early Bird discount typically expires Feb 28 ($50/wk savings). YMCA Camp Orkila + Camp Sealth registration windows open this month — overnight camps. Multi-week discounts often stack with Early Bird.

items.label: March (general public registration)
items.detail: Most Seattle-metro institution camps open general (non-member) registration. Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium typically opens early-mid March. Most popular sessions fill within 2-3 weeks.

items.label: April–May (last call + scholarship windows)
items.detail: Most popular sessions full. Off-the-radar specialty camps still have space. Scholarship application windows often close mid-May — check each org. Many districts publish their summer enrichment lists in April.

items.label: June (late game + cancellations)
items.detail: Some camps add late sessions if demand exists. Cancellation lists at premium camps move quickly — call directly, don't just check website. Parks dept rec camps almost always have space.

sections.title: Scholarship cheat sheet — generous aid most parents don't ask about

items.label: YMCA — sliding scale Price A / Price B
items.detail: All Y branches use a sliding-scale cost structure. You self-select based on household income. No documentation required at registration. Some Ys offer additional financial assistance beyond Price B — ask the membership desk directly. Camp Orkila and other residential Ys have the same structure.

items.label: Pacific Science Center — needs-based scholarships up to 100%
items.detail: Application opens early February (well before general registration). Scholarship windows are SEPARATE from regular registration — apply to both. Bring tax return + proof of income. 100% scholarships exist; partial more common.

items.label: Woodland Park Zoo — scholarships up to 100% in 20% increments
items.detail: Tiered based on income. Application is short. They publish the income brackets — check the FAQ. Apply once per year, valid for all WPZ camps that summer.

items.label: Camp Sealth (Camp Fire CPS) — Camperships
items.detail: Need-based aid called 'Camperships'. Apply 4-6 weeks before session. Particularly generous for 'first-time camper' families. Foster, kinship, and EBT/WIC families get expedited review.

items.label: Point Defiance Zoo — Pierce County resident aid
items.detail: Special scholarship pool for Pierce County residents on EBT/WIC/foster/kinship. Smaller pool but high acceptance rate if eligible.

items.label: Camp Galileo — financial aid + multi-week sibling discounts
items.detail: Up to 75% aid for qualifying families. Multi-week + multi-sibling discounts stack with aid. Apply early — pool is smaller than the museum/zoo programs.

items.label: School district summer programs — often free or near-free
items.detail: Most districts run summer enrichment using federal Title I funds. Eligibility may be income-tested or open to all district kids. Check your district's website starting in March. Often the BEST kept secret in the local market.

sections.title: Nationwide & remote programs — equally available to ANY family

items.label: iD Tech (online + in-person at universities)
items.detail: Coding, game dev, robotics, AI. Online courses for ages 7-19 (live instructor, small groups). In-person held at 50+ university campuses nationwide. Pricing high but financial aid available. Best-known brand in tech ed for kids.

items.label: Camp Galileo (CA + WA expansion + virtual)
items.detail: Also offers Galileo Online — interactive virtual camps for ages 5-12. Project-based, not video lectures. Lower cost than in-person.

items.label: Camp Invention (National Inventors Hall of Fame)
items.detail: Run at thousands of host elementary schools nationwide each summer. STEM + creativity, ages K-6. Pricing modest. Search by zip on their website to find a host school near you.

items.label: Khan Academy Kids + Camps
items.detail: Free K-2 app year-round. Some library systems run Khan-aligned summer programs. Cheapest meaningful enrichment option for early elementary.

items.label: Outschool — small-group online classes (K-12)
items.detail: Marketplace of online classes from independent teachers. Subjects from D&D club to coding to creative writing. Per-class pricing, often $10-30/session. Great for kids with niche interests not served by local options.

items.label: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute (online + Cambridge)
items.detail: Free for accepted students. Targeted at rising 10th-12th but worth knowing about for 7th-8th graders to plan toward.

items.label: AoPS (Art of Problem Solving) Online Math
items.detail: Math classes from Beast Academy (grades 2-5) through advanced HS competition prep. Online or self-paced. The serious math kid pipeline.

items.label: DigiPen Open World Summer Workshops (online + Redmond)
items.detail: Game design, animation, programming. Ages 5-12 + teen tracks. Strong instruction quality.

items.label: MOOC platforms — Coursera, edX, Khan Academy
items.detail: Free university-level content available to motivated middle schoolers. Especially good for kids who finish their grade-level curriculum early.

items.label: Connections Academy + K12 — full virtual public school
items.detail: Free in many states. Year-round option not just summer. Worth considering for kids whose schools aren't a fit, or families with travel flexibility.

sections.title: Sleepaway readiness — is your kid actually ready?

items.label: Green-light signals (start considering 3-5 day sessions)
items.detail: Has done overnights at friends' or relatives' houses without getting homesick. Asks about sleepaway camp themselves. Can dress, brush teeth, and manage basic hygiene independently. Comfortable being out of contact with parents for 24+ hours.

items.label: Yellow-light signals (try a shorter program first)
items.detail: Has had overnight successes but also some homesick episodes. Wants to go but parents are anxious. Manages most independence but needs reminders. Try a 2-3 day camp through the local Y or church first.

items.label: Red-light signals (wait a year)
items.detail: Has anxiety about overnights at relatives'. Has not asked about sleepaway. Struggles with morning routines independently. Nighttime fears or bedwetting still active. Don't push it. Plenty of strong day-camp options through age 12.

items.label: What sleepaway camps actually teach
items.detail: Independence in low-stakes context. Conflict resolution with peers (forced proximity surfaces it). Self-advocacy with adults outside parents. Managing physical fatigue + recovery. Comfort with discomfort (weather, basic accommodations). These compound across years.

items.label: First-timer success patterns
items.detail: Pre-write a few letters together (kids love getting mail). Pre-decide on a comfort item that's not too precious to lose. Talk through what a hard moment might look like + what the kid would do. Don't promise an early pickup — that signals 'this might fail' and erodes confidence.

sections.title: Budget framework — getting maximum value across the summer

items.label: The 60/30/10 frame (a starting heuristic)
items.detail: If you have a fixed summer budget: spend ~60% on a recurring 'anchor' — typically the YMCA / parks dept day camp 3-4 weeks running ($150-300/wk subsidized). Spend ~30% on 1-2 specialty experiences ($400-600 each — the museum camp, the coding camp, the zoo camp). Reserve ~10% for the wildcard — the niche experience the kid asked for, or a weekend mini-camp.

items.label: Multi-summer planning (K-8 arc)
items.detail: K-2: low-stakes exposure across many areas. Cheap day camps + lots of unstructured time. 3-5: discover sustained interests. Add specialty camps in 1-2 areas of demonstrated interest. 6-8: deepen + try sleepaway. Multi-week intensives or residential programs in the area of strongest interest.

items.label: When premium IS worth it
items.detail: When the program creates an experience the kid couldn't replicate at home (boats, horses, theatrical production with peers, 24/7 immersion). When the instructor is genuinely expert (you can tell from the bio + curriculum). When the kid has earned a 'next level' moment after years at lower tiers.

items.label: When premium is NOT worth it
items.detail: When you're paying for the campus brand more than the curriculum. When the kid would happily attend a comparable cheaper option. When you're stretching the family budget. When the kid is reluctantly attending.

items.label: Free + cheap that's actually great
items.detail: Public library summer reading programs (often have weekly events + prizes). Parks dept rec camps. School district summer enrichment (often free with district enrollment). Free museum/library passes (many libraries lend museum passes). Junior ranger badges at national parks ($0).

sections.title: Common parent mistakes (K-8 specifically)

items.label: Over-stacking specialty camps
items.detail: 8 weeks of different 'enrichment' burns kids out. Mix in unstructured time. The downtime is when interests actually consolidate.

items.label: Treating it like college admissions
items.detail: K-8 summers don't appear in college applications. Picking based on 'what looks good' backfires — kids sense the inauthenticity and disengage.

items.label: Skipping the kid's preferences
items.detail: Kids who choose what to attend are happier, more engaged, more likely to develop sustained interests. Even a 6-year-old can rank options.

items.label: Assuming free=bad and expensive=good
items.detail: Parks dept day camps are often excellent. Premium camps are sometimes just well-marketed.

items.label: Not asking about scholarships
items.detail: Most reputable orgs have 50-80% aid available; rarely advertised. Email the camp director directly — application is often shorter than expected.

items.label: Sleepaway too early
items.detail: Pushing a 6-year-old into a week-long overnight because the parent went themselves at that age. Different kid, different generation. Honor the readiness signals.

items.label: Single-track specialization too early
items.detail: A kid who does only soccer camps every summer K-8 won't necessarily play in HS. Variety in K-5 → emerging interest in 6-8 → specialization in 9-12 is the healthier arc.

sections.title: Out-of-the-box hacks most parents miss

items.label: Trade with a friend's family for week-long swap
items.detail: Two families with similar-aged kids each take one week of the other family's kid. Effectively 'free childcare' for a week, kids get the friend-immersion they love, and both families get a week of fewer mouths to feed. Works best ages 7+.

items.label: Volunteer-as-CIT (Counselor In Training) at age 12-14
items.detail: Many camps need junior counselors. Tweens get free or discounted attendance + leadership experience. Apply early — these slots fill faster than camper slots. YMCA, Camp Fire, BGCA all have CIT pipelines.

items.label: Subscribe to a museum at the right tier
items.detail: Not all memberships are equal. Look for the tier that includes 'priority camp registration' — usually $150-200 family-tier upgrade. Pays for itself just from earlier access to popular camps.

items.label: ACA accreditation is a real signal
items.detail: American Camp Association accreditation means health/safety/staff-ratio standards verified annually. Not a fancy badge — actually means something. Free filter at acacamps.org/find-a-camp.

items.label: University youth programs — often hidden gems
items.detail: UW Robinson Center, DigiPen Open World, Stanford EPGY (now Compass), Northwestern Center for Talent Development. Often more substantive than for-profit camps. Check your local research university.

items.label: City parks dept after-school + summer = often the best deal
items.detail: Seattle Parks, Bellevue Parks, Tacoma Metro Parks all run summer day camps for $20-50/day. Quality varies by site, not by department. Visit a site mid-program to assess.

items.label: The 'kid needs a break' permission slip
items.detail: If the kid hasn't had unstructured outdoor time in months, schedule 1-2 unprogrammed weeks. Sounds counterintuitive but kids who get 'permission' to be bored often emerge with new self-directed interests. The opposite of camp.

items.label: Sibling camps at the same site = parent sanity
items.detail: Big multi-program sites (YMCA, large day camps) can take siblings of different ages at once. One drop-off, one pickup, one schedule. Massive parental QoL upgrade vs juggling 3 different camps in 3 locations.

items.label: International summer = often cheaper than US specialty camps
items.detail: Language immersion programs in Mexico/Costa Rica/Spain for ages 8-14 can run $1500-3000 for 2 weeks INCLUDING flights. Compare to a $700/week US specialty camp. Best for kids with at least basic Spanish/French foundation.

items.label: Theater + arts intensives often have surprise scholarships
items.detail: Most regional theaters with kids' programs (Seattle Children's Theatre, ACT Theatre, etc.) have under-applied-for scholarship pools. Even a no-pretense email asking about aid often surfaces options not on the website.

items.label: UW Youth & Teen 'Engineering Challenges' is a GRADES 6-8 course, NOT 9-12 — Wayfinder entry currently mis-tags it as HS-level. Multiple 2-week sessions across summer 2026 (Jun 29-Jul 10, Jul 13-Jul 24, etc.) at UW Seattle, half-day morning (9am-12pm) or afternoon (1pm-4pm). HS-equivalent in the same UW catalog is 'Introduction to Engineering Design & Process' (rising 10-12, full-day 9am-3pm). DATA-QUALITY FIX RECOMMENDED. Tactical timing tip: many 2026 sections in the early-July window are already on Waitlist as of late April — if your top section shows Waitlist, check the later 2-week sessions (Jul 13, Jul 20, Jul 27, Aug 3) which often still show Open
items.detail: (1) DATA-QUALITY FLAG: programs.json entry 'UW Youth & Teen Engineering Challenges' (University of Washington) shows eligibility.grades=['9','10','11','12'], but the actual course is labeled 'Entering Grades 6-8' on the official catalog (https://www.youth-teen.uw.edu/programs/summer-2026-courses). There's also a separate 'Engineering Challenges for Kids' offering for Entering Grades 4-5. The HS-level analogue in the same catalog is 'Introduction to Engineering Design & Process' (Entering Grades 10-12, 9am-3pm full-day). FIX: update-array-items op on programs.json — set eligibility.grades=['6','7','8'] OR change name+grades to match the HS course. Currently parents searching the K-8 endpoint (correctly) miss it because grades=9-12 excludes them, while parents searching HS-grade filters get a course that's actually wrong for their kid. (2) MULTIPLE SESSIONS THROUGHOUT SUMMER: 2-week blocks starting Jun 29, Jul 13, Jul 20, Jul 27, Aug 3 (and likely beyond). Each block has morning (9am-12pm) AND afternoon (1pm-4pm) sections. So there are roughly 8-10 distinct chances to enroll across summer. (3) WAITLIST PRESSURE INDICATOR: as of April 30 2026, multiple early-July Engineering Challenges sections (1B, 2A) were already showing Waitlist. Translate: register the moment you decide; if blocked, immediately scan the later weeks (Jul 13/20/27, Aug 3) before settling for a different course. (4) FOR HS FAMILIES MIS-ROUTED HERE: the UW Y&T HS analogues are 'Introduction to Engineering Design & Process' (rising 10-12, full-day, 2-week, more $$ because full-day) and 'Mission to Mars: Build Your Own Robotic Rover' (rising 9-12, half-day) — those are the actual HS-grade engineering options on the same catalog. (5) FORMAT MIX: catalog includes BOTH in-person at UW Seattle AND online (Zoom) options; Engineering Challenges specifically is in-person UW Seattle only.

items.label: DigiPen Pre-College Summer is $2,995-$3,195/program (Wayfinder shows ~$2,000 — UNDER by $1,000+, DATA-QUALITY FIX REQUIRED). 4-week ONLINE program July 6-31, 2026, M-F 9:30am-4:30pm PST. Hard eligibility: must be at least 16 AND entering Junior or Senior year (or graduated within last 18 months) — the AGE-16 floor is in addition to grade, so a young rising junior who hasn't turned 16 by program start is excluded. GAME PROGRAMMING TRACK additionally requires Algebra 2 completion. HUGE PARENT VALUE that's easy to miss: students who matriculate to DigiPen Institute of Technology within 3 years receive a TUITION CREDIT EQUAL TO THE FULL PRE-COLLEGE TUITION applied to freshman tuition — making the $3K effectively a refundable enrollment hold for DigiPen-bound families. Final transcript IS issued for college applications
items.detail: (1) DATA-QUALITY FLAG #1 — TUITION: Wayfinder cost.amount is 2000 with display '~$2,000 (early bird discount available)'. Actual page lists tuition $2,995 to $3,195 per program (varies by track: Art & Animation, Game Design, Game Programming, Music & Sound). FIX: update-array-items op on programs.json — set cost = { amount:2995, type:'paid', display:'$2,995-$3,195/program (varies by track; tuition credit equal to full pre-college tuition refunded as freshman tuition discount if student matriculates to DigiPen within 3 years)' }. (2) HARD ELIGIBILITY GATES — three of them, ALL must be met: (a) at least 16 years old at program start (NOT just 'rising junior' — the age floor traps young accelerated students), (b) entering Junior or Senior year of high school, OR graduated high school within the last 18 months, (c) GAME PROGRAMMING track only: must have successfully completed Algebra 2. The age-16 + Algebra 2 prereqs aren't in the current Wayfinder entry; parents whose kid is a 15-year-old rising junior should not bother applying to the Programming track. (3) HUGE FINANCIAL TIP — 100% TUITION CREDIT FOR FUTURE DIGIPEN ENROLLEES: 'Any student who successfully completes the Pre-College Program and matriculates to DigiPen Institute of Technology within three years will receive a tuition credit equal to the Pre-College Program tuition to apply toward their first-semester tuition as a freshman.' Translation: if your kid is seriously on a DigiPen path, the $3K is effectively a deposit on freshman year — recouped 1:1. For DigiPen-bound families this changes the value math entirely. For families undecided about DigiPen, treat $3K as the actual sunk cost. (4) FORMAT — ONLINE ONLY: M-F 9:30am-4:30pm PST. Mornings = academic subjects from faculty-level instructors; afternoons = collaborative project lab where students from all 4 tracks (Art, Design, Programming, Music) work together to ship a game. International students welcome — instruction in English, all students must work the 9:30-4:30 PST window. (5) TRANSCRIPT IMPACT (parent-facing): students receive grades for Pre-College classes plus a 'final transcript to include in their college application.' This is a CREDIT-BEARING academic experience that goes on the record — same caveat as Museum of Flight Aero Explorations: a non-passing grade lands on the college-app transcript. Don't enroll unless your kid is committed to engaging seriously M-F all day for 4 weeks. (6) FOUR TRACKS to choose from: Pre-College Art & Animation for Games (Art Foundations + Animation Techniques + Computer Graphics Tools + Game Project Lab); Pre-College Game Design (Principles of Game Design + Applied CS + Interactive Narrative + Game Project Lab); Pre-College Game Programming (Applied CS + Applied Math + Applied Physics + Game Project Lab — needs Algebra 2); Pre-College Music & Sound Design (Music Theory + Music History + Fundamentals of Music & Sound Design + Game Project Lab — recommend prior instrument experience). (7) REGISTRATION: 'OPEN' as of April 30 2026 — register at https://academy.digipen.edu/admissions/registration/. Tech requirements vary by track (some not Mac compatible — check before purchasing hardware).

items.label: UW Changemakers in Computing (CiC) — FREE summer program at UW Allen School for ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED and/or FUTURE FIRST-GEN rising juniors/seniors at WA HS only — applicants without that demographic story should not bother and should pivot to AiC High School Award (different track) or paid Allen School summer courses (open to any HS-grad-of-8th-grade-by-June-30 student via UW Summer Sessions)
items.detail: (1) The Wayfinder entry shows grades 11-12 + free + WA-only — accurate, but the program is NOT 'open to all rising juniors/seniors with a CS interest.' Allen School page is explicit: 'CiC aims to increase the participation of economically disadvantaged and/or future first-generation college students in computer science and engineering.' Application without a clear demonstrable story on either axis is a near-certain pass. Parents should not let their kid spend a weekend on this app if they're full-pay 2nd-gen. (2) BACKUP TRACK at the same source page parents miss: 'Aspirations in Computing (AiC) High School Award' — different program, 9th-12th, computing-related achievements, applications open NOW via Aspirations.org, NCWIT-affiliated, no economic-need filter. Treat as parallel safety. (3) PAID FALLBACK at the same source page: HS students who completed 8th grade by June 30 can ENROLL in regular Allen School summer courses (CSE 121/122/142/143 etc.) for college credit via UW Summer Sessions — costs UW per-credit tuition (~$500-700/credit) but is open to any student regardless of demographics, and the credit transfers. (4) ZERO-COST advising: Allen School holds a prospective-CS info session the FIRST FRIDAY OF EVERY MONTH 3:30-4:30 PT (virtual) — useful regardless of CiC outcome. Direct contact: outreach@cs.washington.edu.

items.label: Museum of Flight Aeronautical Explorations — NOT a summer camp; it's a graded CTE COURSE through Puget Sound Skills Center that goes on transcript + impacts GPA. Up to 2 absences before non-passing grade. WA-RESIDENT-ONLY. June 29-July 17 2026, no class July 3. Apply via PSSC site (NOT museumofflight.org) by May 15. Free + earns 0.5 HS CTE credits, free Connections membership through age 19, AND scholarship eligibility — strong stack of side-benefits for the right family
items.detail: (1) THIS IS A CREDIT-BEARING SEMESTER COURSE COMPRESSED INTO 3 WEEKS — Wayfinder's entry shows it as a 'free CTE program' but doesn't surface that the museum's own page explicitly warns 'Aeronautical Explorations is NOT a summer camp.' It's run through Puget Sound Skills Center, includes graded tests/quizzes/projects, appears on the official high school transcript, and IMPACTS THE STUDENT'S GPA. Parents who treat this as a no-stakes summer enrichment risk a non-passing grade landing on permanent record. (2) THE 2-DAY ABSENCE LIMIT IS ABSOLUTE: 'You are able to miss up to two days before receiving a non-passing grade.' Miss day 3 → it's an F on transcript. Block the entire June 29 - July 17 window before applying; family vacations, sports, conflicting camps must be ruled out. Note: NO class on July 3 (Friday before holiday) is built into the schedule. (3) APPLICATION GOES TO A DIFFERENT WEBSITE: students apply at https://pssc.highlineschools.org/admissions/summer-session — NOT through museumofflight.org. Applicants who try to find an application on the museum's main page will get stuck. Email AeroExplorations@museumofflight.org for step-by-step PSSC instructions. Deadline May 15, 2026. (4) HARD ELIGIBILITY: WA STATE RESIDENTS ONLY — because it's a public school class through PSSC, out-of-state students cannot enroll. Wayfinder's eligibility (rising 9-12) is correct but obscures the residency wall. (5) NO TRANSPORTATION PROVIDED: 8:30am-3:30pm M-F at the Museum (Boeing Field area, 9404 East Marginal Way S, Seattle 98108) and adjacent Raisbeck Aviation HS — light rail Tukwila Int'l + bus is the public option for non-driving families. (6) UNDERRATED PERK STACK: completing AE earns a free 'Connections' educational membership for unlimited Museum admission until age 19, AND eligibility to apply for Museum of Flight scholarships. For aviation-curious families, the side-benefits substantially outvalue the 0.5 credits.

items.label: Seattle U Summer Business Institute — RESIDENTIAL 6-night program at SU campus (Sun July 19-Sat July 25, 2026), $1,500 all-in including housing+meals. Eligibility is AMBIGUOUS on the page itself: header says 'rising 10-12' but program-block says '9th-11th grade' — overlap is rising 10-11 (apply confidently); rising 9 or 12 should email Albers Admissions BEFORE submitting. $50 nonrefundable deposit applied to total. Scholarship app embedded in main app — apply for both at once. Marketed for 'historically marginalized identities' — useful URM/first-gen fit
items.detail: (1) DATA-QUALITY FLAG: Wayfinder lists grades 9-12, but the live SU page contradicts itself — the descriptive intro paragraph says 'rising 10th to 12th graders,' the SBI 2026 dates block says '9th through 11th grade students.' Safest read: rising 10th + 11th apply with confidence; rising 9th and rising 12th email Albers (albers-pcs@seattleu.edu) BEFORE applying to avoid wasted effort. Wayfinder's 9-12 is technically possible but parents should expect possible auto-reject for rising 12. (2) RESIDENTIAL — NOT COMMUTER: 'students will live on-campus during the institute dates (6 evenings).' This is true even for in-Seattle families; there's no day-only option. Means: pack like sleepaway camp, plan transportation logistics for Sunday-July-19 move-in and Saturday-July-25 move-out. (3) COST IS $1,500 ALL-IN, NOT 'VARIES': Wayfinder's display says 'Varies (merit scholarships available)' but the page is concrete — $1,500 cost of attendance includes coursework, curricular excursions, co-curricular activities, AND residential cost. $50 nonrefundable deposit is applied to the $1,500. Scholarships are available as a section WITHIN the program application — fill the scholarship part out at the same time you submit, don't skip thinking it's a separate process. (4) MARGINALIZED IDENTITY MESSAGING: Both the intro AND the dates block reiterate 'students with historically marginalized identities are strongly encouraged to apply' — this is a STRONGER signal than typical DEI language; it suggests SU is actively shaping admit outcomes around URM/first-gen demographic in addition to merit. Parents whose kid fits should lean into that narrative in the application essay; full-pay non-URM applicants should not necessarily count this out but should expect competitive headwinds. (5) ALBERS BUSINESS SCHOOL HOST: program is hosted by Albers School of Business and Economics — meaningful for kids targeting Albers undergrad later (admissions can see your prior engagement).

items.label: ACAP Seattle Residency Week — FREE 1-week OVERNIGHT residency at UW (housing + meals included, transit excluded), open to ANY WA HS rising soph/jr/sr (no district restriction unlike UW Eng Academy/WANIC), Feb-early-April rolling app + 'until full' so apply Feb not April; biggest hidden benefit is YEAR-LONG mentor pairing post-program
items.detail: (1) THIS IS AN OVERNIGHT residency, not a day program — Wayfinder's entry doesn't make this clear. Students stay on the UW Seattle campus for the week with housing + food included; parents need to plan for actual sleepaway logistics (toiletries, week of clothes, dorm bedding policy — confirm with ACAP). (2) ELIGIBILITY IS UNUSUALLY BROAD for a free WA HS pre-college program: any student enrolled at any Washington State high school who will be a sophomore, junior, or senior the FOLLOWING school year. NO Seattle-only restriction (unlike UW Engineering Academy which is Greater-Seattle-only) and NO district consortium restriction (unlike DigiPen WANIC's 7-district gate). Suburban + Eastern WA + rural families are eligible. Admission is 'prioritized for applicants considered to be underrepresented in the accounting field' — first-gen, BIPOC, and low-income applicants should weight this program heavily. (3) APPLICATION TIMING IS DEADLINE-PLUS-FIRST-COME: window is 'early February through early April, OR until the program is full' — meaning April-procrastinators may find the door already shut even if their app would have been competitive. Submit in the Feb half of the window, not April. Online-only application; no paper. (4) FREE INCLUDES: on-campus housing, all food, all program activities, accounting-firm site-visit logistics. PARENTS PAY: transportation to/from UW Seattle for drop-off and pick-up. A FULLY-REFUNDABLE deposit may be requested AFTER acceptance to hold the spot — so 'free' is genuinely free; the deposit returns. (5) BIGGEST UNDERMARKETED BENEFIT: every participant is matched with a mentor from the accounting profession during Residency Week, and that mentorship continues for AT LEAST ONE FULL YEAR after the program ends. items.label: UW Materials Science Camp HS — Free 6-day program July 6-11 2026 at UW Seattle, but ONLY for CURRENT 10th graders (rising 11th, NOT 9-12); apply Feb 1-Mar 15, includes a Saturday 9:30-2 session most parents miss; day camp = no housing, students pay own transit + bring own lunch
items.detail: (1) NARROW GRADE GATE most parents miss: Wayfinder shows eligibility.grades = 9/10/11/12, but the actual program eligibility is ONLY students who are currently 10TH GRADE (sophomore) during the academic year of application — i.e. only RISING JUNIORS attend. Current 9th, 11th, and 12th graders are NOT eligible, period. Programs.json entry should be updated to grades=['10'] (or eligibility note 'must be sophomore during application year only'). Applying as a 9th or 11th grader = automatic rejection. (2) DATES ARE LOCKED: July 6-11, 2026 at UW Seattle MSE department. Schedule is M-F 9:00am-4:30pm + a SATURDAY 9:30am-2:00pm session most families miss when planning July weekends — block the Saturday too. (3) DAY CAMP — NO HOUSING. Students must arrange daily transportation to/from UW Seattle Mon-Sat. Tip: kids 18-and-under ride King County Metro / Sound Transit / Community Transit FREE in WA via Youth Ride Free; mention this to families considering the program but worried about Seattle parking/cost. (4) NO LUNCH PROVIDED — students bring their own or bring money to eat on UW Ave (the Ave has fast options under $15). Worth noting because most other free WA HS programs (UW Eng Academy, WANIC) actually DO provide food. (5) APPLICATION WINDOW IS TIGHT: opens Feb 1 2026, closes 5:00pm March 15 2026 (no rolling, hard deadline), notifications by April 1 — about 2 weeks BEFORE most other WA programs make their decisions, so families using this as a 'safety yes' get an early data point. Required materials: 300-word essay, unofficial HS transcript emailed in PDF to matcamp@uw.edu, and a single online application with applicant + guardian + school info. (6) PREFERRED (not required): 3.0 GPA, basic algebra/chemistry/physical science background, college/career interest in materials/engineering. Prior engineering experience NOT required and U.S. CITIZENSHIP NOT REQUIRED — this is one of the rare WA HS programs explicitly open to international students living locally. items.label: UW Engineering Academy — 2026 application is CLOSED; the 2027 cycle opens in March (no rolling app, no waitlist), 1-week intensive July 20-24 2026 at UW Seattle 10am-4pm in-person, students arrange own transportation

items.label: DigiPen WANIC Summer — STRICT consortium-only eligibility (7 specific Eastside districts: Bellevue / Issaquah / Lake Washington / Mercer Island / Northshore / Riverview / Snoqualmie Valley); LOTTERY placement, 2026 application closed Apr 23 with no exceptions, fail = no entry until 2027
items.detail: (1) HARD GATE most parents miss: this is a WANIC Skill Center program — a regional CTE cooperative — so enrollment is restricted to students in 7 specific Northeast King County districts (Bellevue, Issaquah, Lake Washington, Mercer Island, Northshore, Riverview, Snoqualmie Valley). items.label: Washington Aerospace Scholars (WAS) — Phase 1 is FREE & open to all WA juniors; the $1,850 fee only applies to Phase 2 acceptees, with 50% deposit due AFTER acceptance and up to 100% tuition assistance for government-aid families
items.detail: WAS is the rare WA STEM program where the front door is genuinely free and selection is performance-based, not application-based. items.label: UW STEP (Students Exploring Pharmacy) — $200 fee is NON-REFUNDABLE at acceptance, free/reduced-lunch families get partial-or-full waiver, and recommender link arrives 5-7 business days AFTER you submit
items.detail: UW School of Pharmacy's STEP is a 4-day immersion (Mon Jul 13 - Thu Jul 16, 2026) for grades 9-12 with priority to rising juniors and seniors — but four under-published facts that change the application game: (1) THE $200 FEE IS NON-REFUNDABLE AND DUE AT ACCEPTANCE CONFIRMATION — once you accept, you cannot back out without forfeiting. Includes all activities, materials, daily lunch. Plan for the full $200 the day you accept. (2) FREE/REDUCED-PRICE SCHOOL LUNCH STUDENTS QUALIFY FOR A SCHOLARSHIP — partial OR full waiver of the $200 fee plus daily lunch. The scholarship pathway is implicit in the application — flag it in your personal statement so the admissions team can match aid to your file. (3) RECOMMENDER LINK TIMING: your recommender (teacher, counselor, advisor, or supervisor) gets the email link 5-7 BUSINESS DAYS AFTER you submit the application form — so warn them BEFORE you submit so they can watch for it during finals/AP-testing season when teacher inboxes get buried. Please include any personal or lived experiences that may have shaped your interests.' The 'lived experiences' clause is the differentiator — first-gen healthcare interest, family member in pharmacy, watching a relative manage chronic conditions all are signal-rich; generic 'I want to help people' answers are forgettable. (5) DEADLINE: April 30, 2026; notifications early June. (6) Disability accommodations need 10-day advance notice via UW DSO at 206-543-6450 / dso@uw.edu. items.label: Camp Galileo Bellevue (STEAM Day Camp) — three-tier discount stack ($110+/wk via Sept-prior Early Enrollment, $50/wk via Feb 28 Early Bird, then $25/wk multi-week + $100 off 6 weeks)
items.detail: Galileo's discount structure has THREE separate stacking tiers that most parents only learn about one at a time — and the cheapest tier closes 9 months before camp starts. (1) EARLIEST + DEEPEST: Buy 2026 camp weeks by Sept 30, 2025 = $100+/wk off list price (Galileo's 'Early Enrollment'). For 2027 planning, this means parents who lock in by Sept 30, 2026 will save the most — but you have to commit to specific weeks before the 2027 calendar is fully published. (2) MIDDLE TIER: Enroll by Feb 28, 2026 = $50/wk off ('Early Bird') + free cancellation through Jan 31 + priority friend placement (huge for shy kids — first dibs on requesting a buddy in the same group) + the Early Bird pin. (3) LIVE-ALL-SUMMER STACK: $25/wk off after the first week (multi-week) AND $100 off any 6-week purchase. A family doing 6 weeks at Galileo can stack $25×5 weeks ($125) + $100 = $225 off in stack discounts ALONE, before any tier-1 or tier-2 discount. Extended care is sneakily expensive for what's effectively babysitting: $36/wk morning, $72/wk afternoon, $90/wk both (on 4-day weeks — adjust for full weeks). Galileo serves grades K-10 (broader than the K-5 their Bellevue page foregrounds), and offers 'sliding scale scholarships' in every served community — meaning the YMCA Price A/B model, not pure need-based — so middle-income families can apply too. (Source: galileo-camps.com/our-camps/locations/bellevue/ + galileo-camps.com/summer-adventures-await/, harvested 2026-04-28.)

items.label: IslandWood — TWO campuses (Bainbridge AND Brightwater Education Center in Woodinville), 2026 financial-aid pool was EXHAUSTED before April; aid applicants now go on a wait-only list
items.detail: Two pieces of intel that change the calculus for King County families: (1) BRIGHTWATER (WOODINVILLE) IS THE EASTSIDE-FRIENDLY OPTION — IslandWood runs outdoor day camps both at the 255-acre Bainbridge Island campus AND at the Brightwater Education Center in Woodinville. Same IslandWood programming, same naturalist-led environmental-ed model, NO ferry. Most King County / Eastside / Snohomish County parents only know about Bainbridge (which requires a pre-7am rush to the Seattle ferry terminal, $20+ ferry walk-on roundtrip per parent if dropping in person, or a ~50-min drive via the Tacoma Narrows). Brightwater is a 25-min drive from Bellevue, 35-min from Seattle. If your family is east of the Cut, default to checking Brightwater availability FIRST — it's both more practical and often less competitive than the marquee Bainbridge campus. (2) FINANCIAL-AID FUNDS GONE BY APRIL 2026 — IslandWood's financial-assistance pool for summer 2026 was fully allocated before the end of April. New applicants can submit a need form, but the form just adds you to a 'if more funds become available, we'll reach out' wait-only list. Practical implication: IslandWood opens registration Feb 28 — families who NEED aid must apply for both registration AND aid that DAY, not after the kid finishes their school year. By April it's too late. Standard cancellation tiers still apply (Apr 3 = full refund less $100 processing fee, Jun 5 = 50% refund, after Jun 5 = no refund except medical). (Source: islandwood.org/outdoor-summer-day-camps-2026/ via WebSearch cache, harvested 2026-04-28.)

items.label: Seattle Aquarium Marine Summer Camp — per-week capacity is HARD-CAPPED at 20 (Micro-biologists) or 25 (others) with 2 reserved scholarship seats per session; teen track DROPPED for 2026; loading zone is NOT for drop-off
items.detail: Three under-published facts from the Aquarium camp page that change parent strategy: (1) SCHOLARSHIP SEATS ARE A SEPARATE POOL — Micro-biologists (ages 4-5, 9:30am-12:30pm) has 20 spots: 18 public/member + 2 RESERVED scholarship; all other camps (Octopus odyssey 6-7, Fin-tastic sharks 8-9, Evolution in action 10-12) have 25 spots: 23 public + 2 RESERVED scholarship. Translation for parents needing aid: even if a session shows SOLD OUT in public registration, your scholarship application is for a DIFFERENT pool of 2 dedicated seats — apply for scholarship even if the public sold out. The Aquarium explicitly says a sold-out session does NOT affect scholarship applications. (2) CONFIRMED 2026 PRICING + EXTENDED CARE PRESSURE — Micro-biologists half-day = $215/wk. Octopus/Sharks/Evolution full-day = $525/wk. Members get 10% off. Before-care 8:30-9:15am OR after-care 4-4:45pm = $25/single session, $100 for one of (B or A) for the week, $200/wk for BOTH B+A. Stacking both adds 38% to the $525 base — for a working parent doing 8 weeks, that's $1,600 in just extended-care fees. If your work permits a 9:30am drop-off and 4pm pickup, skip B+A entirely; if not, the single-session $25 may pencil better than the weekly bundle for sporadic days. (3) HARD AGE CUTOFFS + DROPPED 13-14 TRACK + NO CURBSIDE DROP-OFF — Aquarium DROPPED the 13-14 year-old camp this year due to past low demand, so families who relied on it as their middle-school go-to need an alternative (Pacific Science Center, Burke Museum, or BIOQUEST programs run older). They will NOT accept kids outside their designated age range — 'mature for their age' arguments are explicitly refused per FAQ. The loading zone in front of Pier 59 is NOT for drop-off or pickup — caregivers MUST walk campers into the classrooms each day, and at pickup MUST present a government-issued ID. Parents who're used to curb-and-go at school will hit a 5-min friction every day. Counselor-to-camper ratios are strong: ~5 staff (1 ops lead + 1 lead counselor + 3 counselors) per 25 kids = 1:5. (Source: seattleaquarium.org/explore-the-aquarium/programs/marine-summer-camp/, harvested 2026-04-28.)

items.label: City of Vancouver WA Parks & Rec — registration deadline is 9 a.m. Thursday before each camp week, ALL waitlists wipe July 6, aftercare exists ONLY at Marshall Camp
items.detail: Five concrete pieces of intel from the official 2026 Vancouver WA Parks & Rec recreation-camps page (covers Marshall Youth Day Camp, Fircrest Youth Day Camp, Access to Recreation Camp): (1) HARD REGISTRATION DEADLINE — registration closes at 9 a.m. on Thursday the week prior to the start of each camp week. Plan only available for Marshall, Fircrest, and Access to Recreation Camp. Failed-payment processing fee = $5 per week. (5) EVERYBODY PLAYS! SCHOLARSHIP HAS A CITY-LIMITS GAP — the 50% tuition scholarship requires primary address WITHIN Vancouver city limits. Families in Hazel Dell, Salmon Creek, Felida, or Camas (just outside city limits) DON'T qualify even though they're a 5-min drive away — important for parents who think 'we live in Vancouver' but actually live in unincorporated Clark County. Refund deadline = 4 weeks before camp start. ePACT participant form must be completed before attending. (Source: cityofvancouver.us/government/department/parks-recreation-and-cultural-services/recreation-activities/recreation-camps/, harvested 2026-04-28.)

items.label: Washington MESA College Prep — most parents miss the 'Summer Math Scholars' bridge for incoming 9th graders + the Boeing/Weyerhaeuser scholarships up to $2,500
items.detail: Three under-marketed assets in the FREE Washington MESA College Prep Program (UW Office of Minority Affairs partnership, 6th-12th grade, low-income / first-gen / racial-ethnic-minority eligibility): (1) SUMMER MATH SCHOLARS — a 3-week summer program designed specifically for incoming 9th graders to enter HS placed ABOVE their current grade level in math. Most parents searching for 'summer math camp' for rising-9th never find this because it's buried under 'College Prep Program' rather than marketed as a summer offering. Real impact: a kid who finishes 8th-grade Algebra 1 can land in Geometry-or-higher freshman year, which compounds into Calc-by-junior year — a hugely valuable college-app signal. (2) BOEING + WEYERHAEUSER SCHOLARSHIPS UP TO $2,500 EACH — both named industry scholarships are reserved for MESA students. Most families don't know these exist, let alone that you can apply only by being a MESA participant. Two named-corp scholarships from PNW industry giants is a stronger college-app narrative than a generic 'community service award.' (3) MESA DAY PIPELINE = COLLEGE-APP-READY COMPETITION TRACK — every MESA Day flows: 6 WA regional competitions (math + science + engineering challenges) -> State competition -> ONE team per challenge represents WA at the National USA-MESA Engineering Design Competition. Parents looking for an 'authentic' STEM extracurricular that produces tangible quantifiable results (regional/state/national placements) should know this exists for FREE inside MESA without any of the $1500 USACO-camp / $3000 robotics-club costs. Year-round enrollment via the local MESA chapter at the participating school — check washington.edu/omad/washington-mesa for which WA schools have a chapter (heavily concentrated in Title-I-served districts). (Source: washington.edu/omad/washington-mesa/college-prep-program, harvested 2026-04-28.)

items.label: Launch Learning — NOT free in 2026 ($303-$505/wk Seattle, $256-$320/wk Renton); 10% discount expires May 1; Renton opens 6:00am for early-shift parents
items.detail: Four corrections + insights for Launch Learning Summer 2026 — many existing parent guides (including ours pre-harvest) call this program 'free / heavily subsidized,' but the official 2026 tuition page contradicts that: (1) PRICING IS REAL: Seattle School-Age Wks 3-9 = $505/wk (Beacon Hill/Highland Park/Kimball/Madrona). Renton (Cascade Vista) Wks 3-8 = $320/wk. That's a $185/wk gap (37% cheaper at Renton) — for SE King County families willing to commute, the 8-week savings is ~$1,480. Preschool: Seattle Miller Annex full-day = $2,215/mo, Renton Cascade Vista 5-day full-day preschool = $1,750/mo. (2) 10% ALL-SUMMER-WEEKS DISCOUNT (school-age only) — register your child for ALL summer weeks by MAY 1 to lock in the discount. (3) RENTON CASCADE VISTA OPENS AT 6:00 AM and runs to 6:30 PM (Mon-Fri), uniquely accommodating swing-shift / very-early-shift parents — Seattle sites are 8am-6pm only. items.label: UW K-12 Engineering Outreach — most 'free' UW programs are HS-only; for K-8 the entry points are Discovery Days (4th-8th, 10,000 visitors) + Engineering Ambassadors school visits
items.detail: Three filters K-8 parents should apply when navigating UW College of Engineering's 'K-12' programs page (the umbrella covers very different age targets that all say 'K-12'): (1) ENGINEERING DISCOVERY DAYS is the marquee K-8 entry point — FREE 2-day spring event on UW campus, ~10,000 visitors annually, explicitly 4th-8th GRADE oriented (NOT K-12 broadly despite the umbrella name). Hands-on activities run by UW engineering students/faculty. Watch the engr.washington.edu calendar in Jan-Feb for the date drop. Best for: a kid who's STEM-curious but hasn't committed; one full afternoon of free exploration with no application. (2) MOST OTHER 'FREE' UW PROGRAMS ARE HS-ONLY. Engineering Academy (5-day summer camp) = HS only. Changemakers in Computing (CIC) = rising juniors/seniors only. Center for Neurotechnology Young Scholars = HS. DO-IT Scholars = HS with disabilities. Parents of K-8 kids who try to apply waste the slot — not eligible. The K-8 path is Discovery Days + the SEPARATE 'UW Summer Youth Programs' umbrella (full-day camps + half-day short courses, paid, broader age range). (3) HIDDEN GEM — ENGINEERING AMBASSADORS. Free service where UW engineering undergrads come to YOUR K-12 SCHOOL to do in-classroom presentations and hands-on activities. Most parents and teachers don't know it exists. Bring it to your PTA: an EA visit costs the school $0, gives kids real-engineer role models, and works especially well for under-resourced or rural districts that don't have a tech corridor in commute distance. Email request via engr.washington.edu/k12 → Engineering Ambassadors. Bonus: HCDE-led K-12 Outreach Workshops specifically target underrepresented and resource-constrained Seattle-area schools — ask your school's principal or district equity office to opt in. (Source: engr.washington.edu/k12, harvested 2026-04-27.)

items.label: Camp Korey (Mt. Vernon, WA) — ASD/ADHD/ADD as PRIMARY diagnosis are NOT eligible (most-missed parent rejection trigger) + ages 7-17 overnight camper / 5-17 family + strict immunization table
items.detail: Five hard-truth eligibility facts that re-route a lot of families away from disappointment: (1) CRITICAL ELIGIBILITY GATE: Camp Korey does NOT serve Autism, ADHD, or ADD as a PRIMARY diagnosis — the camp is for chronic life-altering medical conditions that require ongoing medical care/follow-up treatment (cancer, blood disorders, neurological conditions, etc.). Kids with ASD/ADHD/ADD ARE accepted if they ALSO have another qualifying medical diagnosis. Many parents apply assuming 'free camp for kids with disabilities' and are denied. Email admissionsteam@campkorey.org or call (425) 616-7238 to confirm eligibility BEFORE filling out CampSite. (2) AGE GATE: Overnight Summer Camper (kid-only, no parents) is ages 7-17. Overnight Family Camp (whole family up to 6 immediate members) is ages 5-17 — under-5 siblings need a phone call to admissions to confirm what family experience looks like. (3) ALL applications are reviewed by program + medical teams; acceptance is NOT first-come-first-served — it's based on space, healthcare needs, and staffing ratios. Camper must be able to communicate needs in some way and function in a group setting. (4) STRICT IMMUNIZATION TABLE: 2 doses MMR, 2 doses Varicella (or documented chickenpox/shingles history), 5-dose DTaP series + Tdap booster (last booster within 10 years of camp session), 3 doses Hep B, 4 doses Polio, ANNUAL flu Nov-Apr (and may be required other times). Immunocompromised kids unable to receive live vaccines (transplant, chemo within last year, high-dose steroids 14+ days, immunosuppressants, CD4<15%) get exemptions for MMR/Varicella; positive titers also acceptable. Plan vaccine schedule months in advance. (5) Application is via 'CampSite' software (create family account once, edit forms anytime). 100% free including travel, meals, lodging, on-site medical staff. Family camps year-round, not just summer. (Source: campkorey.org/camp/camp-korey-faq, harvested 2026-04-27.)

items.label: SPS Expanded Learning Summer — 20:2 ratio + WAITLIST + Parent Appeal + ESY runs SEPARATE program
items.detail: Four things parents miss about Seattle Public Schools' free K-8 summer program: (1) Class size is locked at 20:2 student-to-adult ratio (10:1) — a tighter ratio than most paid camps, which is why the program is so effective for kids who got bumped down to <60th percentile MAP/DIBELS. (2) There IS a Summer Learning WAITLIST — when the May 1 deadline passes and a school's seats are full, your kid can still get on the waitlist (link in the SPS Expanded Learning sidebar) and seats open up regularly through June. (3) The 'Summer Learning Parent Appeal' is a real lever — if your child was assessed as ABOVE the 60th percentile but you have evidence summer slide is a risk (e.g., your kid bombed a recent unit, IEP/504 not yet active, recent move), you can formally appeal placement. (4) ESY (Extended School Year) is run by a SEPARATE department (Special Education, not Expanded Learning) — IEP families get a different application path, breakfast/lunch included, NO 60th-percentile cutoff. Don't confuse the two enrollments. (Source: seattleschools.org/departments/expanded-learning, harvested 2026-04-27.)

items.label: Burke Museum — NO REFUNDS for 2026 camps (hardest-stance in WA cluster)
items.detail: Burke Museum has the strictest refund policy of any major Seattle K-8 camp this year — VERBATIM site language: 'Camp payments are final. We are not able to offer refunds for Burke Camps this year.' Unlike KidsQuest (refunds till May 22 with $50 fee) or Pacific Science Center (sliding-scale refund), Burke is zero-refund from the moment you click pay. Action: only book Burke camps for dates where childcare is 100% locked. Single-day camps (e.g., Dino Trackers Mon Jul 13) are at $100 — losing that to a sick kid is one-week-of-grocery money for many families. If your kid is on the fence, do a Burke gallery visit FIRST before committing. (Source: burkemuseum.org/education/families-and-youth/camps, harvested 2026-04-27.)
items.sourceProvider: Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (UW)
items.sourceName: Burke Museum Summer Camps (Dino Trackers & Paleo Discovery)

items.label: Burke financial assistance — 50% of fee, NOT a full waiver
items.detail: Burke Museum financial assistance covers ONLY 50% of the full program fee — half-discount, not a free spot. (Robinson Center next-door offers FULL waivers for the same income tier; Pacific Science Center waives 100% for SNAP families; Burke is the strictest of the three.) Apply via the Financial Assistance form on burkemuseum.org/education/financial-assistance — staff respond within ~2 weeks, so submit at LEAST 3 weeks before your target camp's registration deadline to avoid losing the spot while waiting on a decision. If approved 50% still doesn't fit your budget, layer Burke aid with a Bezos Family Foundation or Boys & Girls Club summer-camp grant. (Source: burkemuseum.org/education/families-and-youth/camps, harvested 2026-04-27.)

items.label: Burke grade conventions — uses RISING grade (2026/27 school year), not current
items.detail: Burke Museum camps state grade eligibility as 'Grades X-Y in the 2026/27 SCHOOL YEAR' — meaning the grade your child will enter in fall 2026, NOT their current April-2026 grade. Common parent error: a child finishing 3rd grade right now is rising into 4th, so they qualify for the Grades 4-6 'Fossil Detectives' track (NOT the Grades 1-3 'Dino Trackers'). When in doubt, register the rising-grade bracket — most museums in WA follow this same convention but Burke is the only one that publishes it explicitly. Aftercare 3:30-5pm runs $30 extra (already in main note); confirm whether your week has aftercare staffed at registration since not every Burke camp date offers it. (Source: burkemuseum.org/education/families-and-youth/camps, harvested 2026-04-27.)

items.label: Lakeside LEEP — 2026 dates locked + cohort sizes
items.detail: Lakeside Educational Enrichment Program (LEEP) 2026 runs July 6 - July 31, Mon-Fri 9am-3pm. Total cohort is 90 students: 50 rising 6th graders + 40 rising 9th graders, with 1-to-18 student-to-teacher ratio and a counselor in every classroom. Free 4-week summer enrichment for current 5th + 8th graders in Seattle Public Schools. Includes light breakfast + full lunch daily, free First Student bus transportation, and all classroom supplies. (Source: lakesideschool.org/summer/leep, harvested 2026-04-27.)

items.label: Lakeside LEEP — apply via Ravenna, Apr 1 / May 1 / June 1 calendar
items.detail: LEEP application opens April 1, closes May 1, decisions notified May 1, enrollment due June 1 — all via ravenna-hub.com (search 'LEEP' in the School Directory). A complete app needs 5 forms: Family Info, Student Statement, Parent/Guardian Statement, Current School Grades release, and a Behavior/Attendance form from the current school. Late applications case-by-case via LEEP@lakesideschool.org. The 2026-2027 Lakeside admissions cycle is closed — LEEP is a separate process from Lakeside main admissions and is FREE.

items.label: Lakeside LEEP — full attendance required, plan 15-90 min bus rides
items.detail: Accepted LEEP students are EXPECTED to attend the full 4 weeks — known schedule conflicts (family vacations, other camps, summer travel) mean LEEP is not the right fit, per the program. Bus rides add 15-90 minutes each way depending on stop location and Seattle traffic — bus stops are at SPS schools, community centers, and libraries. 92% of 2025 LEEP cohort identified as students of color, 61% qualified for free/reduced lunch, 36 spoke a second language at home — community is intentionally diverse. Voluntary parent contributions accepted but never required.

items.label: UW Youth & Teen — 4 two-week sessions, half-day stacking unlocks full-day childcare
items.detail: UW Youth & Teen Programs 2026 runs as 4 two-week sessions (Jun 29-Jul 10, Jul 13-Jul 24, Jul 27-Aug 7, Aug 10-Aug 21). Each course is HALF-DAY: 9am-12pm (slot 'A') OR 1pm-4pm (slot 'B'). Stack one A + one B course in the same week to make a full day on UW Seattle campus — different course in each slot. Grade buckets are entering 4-5, 6-8, and 9-12 (no K-3). Many courses also offered Online via Zoom as an alternate format.

items.label: UW Youth & Teen — Online courses still Open when UW Seattle is Waitlist
items.detail: As of late April 2026, ~30-40% of UW Seattle in-person courses are already on Waitlist for the early sessions (Jun 29 + Jul 13) — but the SAME-NAMED Online (Zoom) sections are typically still Open. If your child is location-flexible, switching from UW Seattle to Online for the first two sessions gets them in. Hot courses currently waitlist: 3D Design & CAD Modeling, Architectural Studies, Intro to AI & Machine Learning, Mission to Mars, DIY Electronics (1A), Mechanics of Writing for HS. Late summer sessions (Jul 27 + Aug 10) still have wider in-person availability.

items.label: UW Youth & Teen — early-summer hot courses to register at first 2027 opening
items.detail: By April 27, 2026 the following UW Youth & Teen courses are already Waitlisted for week 1 (Jun 29 start): 3D Design & CAD (gr 4-5 + 6-8), Architectural Studies, Intro to AI & ML (both slots), DIY Electronics (1A morning), Hello World CS/Robotics/AI Literacy (1A), HS Entrepreneurship Startup Lab, Inside the Courthouse only the morning slot, and Innovation Lab Robotics & Coding for Kids. If any of these are priorities for your child for 2027, calendar the moment registration opens (typically late January / early February for the new summer) — they sell out fastest by far. Mathematical/data viz courses + most online sections still have room well into April.

items.label: iD Tech UW Seattle — March 1 is the cancellation cliff
items.detail: iD Tech's refund policy has a hard cliff at March 1: cancel BEFORE March 1 = full refund of all amounts paid. Cancel after March 1 but 28+ days before your session = refund minus a $250 per-week cancellation charge. Within 28 days of the session start = NO refund at all. Free unlimited course/week changes (no fees) are also locked out at the 28-day mark. If you're booking a $1,149/wk K-8 day camp or a $4,999 Teen Academy, plan your final commitment around Feb to keep full optionality.
items.sourceName: iD Tech Camps at UW Seattle

items.label: iD Tech UW Seattle — auto-stack $50 course/sibling + $25 referral discounts
items.detail: iD Tech automatically applies $50 off for each ADDITIONAL course or sibling beyond your first registration (no code needed — applied at checkout). Separately, after you register you receive a Refer-a-Friend code good for 10 friends; you and the referred family each get $25 credit. Two kids × 2 weeks each = $150 in stacked savings most parents miss. Payment plans start at $375 down with monthly installments — useful for families spreading the $1,149+/wk day camp cost.
items.sourceName: iD Tech Camps at UW Seattle

items.label: iD Tech Teen Academy — 2-week portfolio is the real college-app ROI
items.detail: The 2-week iD Tech Teen Academy at UW (ages 13-18, $4,999+, overnight only) ends with a portfolio project + iD Tech diploma + transcript explicitly designed for college apps, internships, and resumes — that's the differentiator vs the 1-week camps. Teens also get more autonomy, dorm life, optional weekend stays (supervised but not instruction-focused), Pike Place + Space Needle + MoPOP excursions, and Friday Family Showcase to present their final project. If you're paying premium for a high schooler, the portfolio is the durable artifact — for K-8 the day camp at $1,149/wk hits a different ROI (skill exposure, not portfolio).
items.sourceName: iD Tech Camps at UW Seattle

items.label: Aquarium of the Pacific — 2026 sessions sell out same day
items.detail: All five 2026 Aquarium of the Pacific summer camp tracks (Fish Fry, Sea Squirts, Ocean Adventure, Junior Biologist, Coastal Explorer) were SOLD OUT within ~24 hours of public registration (March 12, 2026). Members register one day earlier (March 11) — calendar that date for 2027.

items.label: Cabrillo Marine Aquarium — 4-day camp for $85 (city-subsidized)
items.detail: Cabrillo Marine Aquarium (San Pedro) charges only $85 ($77 Friends member) for the 4-day grades 1-8 summer marine-science sessions — including a program t-shirt — because it's operated by LA City Recreation & Parks. That's roughly 1/4 the cost of comparable LA-area aquarium camps. Registration opens March 2 (members) / March 16 (non-members).

items.label: Fleet Science Center (San Diego) — 4-day weeks save ~$80-$100
items.detail: Fleet Science Center in Balboa Park prices its 4-day camp weeks (e.g., June 15-18, 2026) at $340 non-member / $280 member full-day, vs. $425/$350 for 5-day weeks. Half-day TK-K 4-day weeks are $180/$160. Picking holiday-week 4-day sessions saves $85 (full) or $45 (half).

items.label: MOSAC Sacramento — Family Duo membership unlocks Camp Curiosity early-access
items.detail: SMUD MOSAC's Camp Curiosity (Sacramento) requires Family Duo level membership or above to access the member discount AND the 2-week-earlier registration window (March 18-20 vs. April 1-3, 2026). Lower membership tiers do NOT qualify. Member discount is $20/week (K half-day) up to $20/week (Design Lab specialty) — pays for itself in 1-2 camps for repeat families.

items.label: Discovery Cube — early pick-up option saves $100-$130/week
items.detail: Discovery Cube OC + LA offer an optional 2pm early pick-up for K-2 camps (vs. 4pm standard). Member rate drops from $365-$410 to $265-$290; non-member rate from $400-$445 to $285-$315. That's $100-$130/week savings if your child can be done by 2pm. Older campers (3-5) don't get this option.

items.label: NHM LA Adventures in Nature — afternoon extended care is $75/week add-on
items.detail: NHM Adventures in Nature day camp (LA, Exposition Park) ends at 3pm. Afternoon extended care 3-5pm is an add-on at $75/week — not bundled. Working parents add it; weekly tuition becomes $475 non-member / $435 member. Cheaper than full-day equivalents at peer LA museums.

items.label: Math Kangaroo USA — Late-fee penalty is nearly 2x
items.detail: Math Kangaroo USA charges $18 for standard registration (Sep 15 - Dec 31) but jumps to $35 if you wait until Jan 1 - Feb 1 — almost double. The contest is the same. (As of 2026-04-26.) Test day 2026 is Mar 19.

items.label: MOEMS — Individual students cannot enroll directly
items.detail: MOEMS Math Olympiad only accepts SCHOOL TEAMS, not individual students. If a school does not run MOEMS, parents need to organize through a homeschool co-op, after-school program, or PTA. 2026-27 enrollment opens May 2026.

items.label: KiwiCo — Annual plan saves ~25-30% over monthly
items.detail: KiwiCo monthly is ~$24/mo but the 12-month plan drops to ~$18.50/mo (save ~$66/yr per child) and 6-month to ~$19.95/mo. Many parents subscribe month-to-month and miss this; the discount is on the same crates.

items.label: MEL Science — First box 60% off during promo windows
items.detail: MEL Science runs first-box 60%-off promos during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and parts of summer — drops month-1 cost from $29.90 to ~$12. Annual plan is also '12 months for the price of 8' — equivalent to ~33% off.

items.label: ChessKid — Free tier covers everything that matters for under-rated kids
items.detail: ChessKid Gold is $49/yr for lessons + puzzles, but FREE tier already includes unlimited play, slow chess, basic puzzles, and the FunMaster Mike video series. Most kids under USCF 800 don't need Gold. Many local chess clubs sponsor Gold memberships for active club members.

items.label: Prodigy Math — Paid tiers are 100% cosmetic, not content
items.detail: Prodigy Math Level Up ($9.95/mo) and Ultimate ($14.95/mo) DO NOT unlock any additional math content — all 45,000+ curriculum-aligned questions are free. Paid tiers only unlock cosmetic upgrades, member zones, and progress dashboards. Don't pay unless your child specifically motivates around the rewards.

items.label: Steve & Kate's Camp — auto-refund unused passes is unusual leverage
items.detail: Buy 15+ Day Passes ($114/day) instead of a Summer Pass; unused passes are AUTOMATICALLY refunded after summer. Most parents over-buy fearing waste — this model removes that risk entirely. Bay Area + LA only.

items.label: Lawrence Hall of Science — 2-week sessions vs 1-week peers
items.detail: Lawrence Hall (UC Berkeley) deliberately runs 2-week sessions instead of the standard 1-week. Better content depth + camper community, but parents need to plan around the longer commit. $625–$950/wk; financial aid app is open for 2026.

items.label: California Science Center — half + afternoon = full day flexibility
items.detail: CSC Hands-On Science Camp lets you mix-and-match a morning class + afternoon class to make a full day. Extended care (8–9am & 3–5pm) is $110/wk for members vs $120 non — membership pays for itself if you need wraparound care all summer.

items.label: Birch Aquarium — Scripps scholarships are quietly available
items.detail: Birch Aquarium summer camps ($250–$600/wk) have needs-based scholarships not advertised on the main page. Email birchaquariumprogram@ucsd.edu BEFORE registration windows close — Scripps backs the program so funding is more reliable than a typical aquarium.

items.label: The Tech Interactive — IMAX + after-hours exhibits included
items.detail: CAMP at The Tech (rising grades 3–6) includes IMAX Dome films and exclusive after-hours exhibit access in tuition. Hidden value vs comparable 1-week STEM camps. 8 sessions June 15 – Aug 7, 2026; cost not on landing page — direct contact required.

items.label: Synthesis — Two products under one brand
items.detail: Synthesis sells two completely different products under the same brand: Synthesis Teams ($95/mo, ages 8-14, weekly cohort problem-solving) and Synthesis Tutor ($25-30/mo, K-5, AI math tutor). Many parents land on the wrong product page — verify which one you want before signing up. Tutor at synthesis.com/tutor vs cohort at synthesis.com/teams. Confirmed 2026-04-26.

items.label: Mathnasium — Summer pricing varies by franchise
items.detail: Same 8-session summer package can range $269-$349+ for elementary depending on location, and 2-hour sessions roughly double that ($538-$698 elementary). Always ask the local center for BOTH 1-hour AND 2-hour bundle quotes — per-hour rate often drops with the longer block. New-student summer enrollment fee $49 or $99 depending on package. Confirmed 2026-04-26.

items.label: Code Ninjas — Half-day blocks stack into full-day at one center
items.detail: Code Ninjas summer camps run as half-day blocks (8:30am-12pm OR 12:30pm-4pm). Stacking BOTH blocks at the same franchise gets you full-day coverage at one location — but it's not advertised on the booking page. Ask the local center to combine bookings, which often unlocks a small lunch-bridge accommodation. Confirmed 2026-04-26.

items.label: Connected Camps — 90 min/day, NOT a childcare solution
items.detail: Connected Camps' weeklong online courses are 90 minutes/day for 5 days — total 7.5 hours of instruction, not full-day camp. Excellent enrichment supplement (Minecraft, Roblox, esports, ages 8-13), but parents expecting daycare-equivalent coverage will be surprised. Pair with another program if you need full-day coverage. Confirmed 2026-04-26.

items.label: Outschool — Quality is per-teacher, not per-platform
items.detail: Outschool is a marketplace — Outschool keeps 30%, teachers set their own prices and curriculum. A 'great Outschool class' is really a great individual teacher. Sort by reviews, watch the teacher's intro video, check their other listings before enrolling. Class quality has more to do with the teacher than the Outschool brand. Confirmed 2026-04-26.

items.label: Brain Chase — Async + travel-friendly summer learning
items.detail: Brain Chase ($179 early bird / $199 standard) runs June 15 - July 17, 2026 — 5 weeks, ~4 hrs/week academic. Async pacing means kids can do it during summer travel; the global treasure-hunt narrative (real buried prize) wraps academic work as a quest. Best fit grades 2-8. Confirmed 2026-04-26.

items.label: Mystery Science — Free trial extended through June 30, 2026 (no card)
items.detail: Mystery Science (mysteryscience.com) currently has a free trial through June 30, 2026 with no credit card required, giving access to select K-5 units, mini-lessons, and hands-on activities. Best low-friction summer-science option for elementary parents to try before committing to a paid family plan (added 2026-04-26).

items.label: Generation Genius — Free trial is 14 days no-card, NOT 30
items.detail: Generation Genius (generationgenius.com) advertises a 14-day free trial that requires zero credit card upfront — easier-than-most onramp. After 14 days you must add payment to continue. Subscription pricing is not on the public landing — must email or visit /subscribe to see (added 2026-04-26).

items.label: Camp CrunchLabs — Auto-rolls into monthly at $27.45 after 12-week summer
items.detail: Camp CrunchLabs ships 12 weekly Build Boxes for $329.40 (~$27.45/wk), but at week 13 you are auto-enrolled into the regular Build Box month-to-month subscription at $27.45/month. Parents who want only the summer experience must cancel before the auto-renew (added 2026-04-26).

items.label: Camp Wonderopolis — Fully free with no payment ever (NCFL-funded)
items.detail: Camp Wonderopolis (camp.wonderopolis.org) by the National Center for Families Learning is 100% free, no credit card, no upgrade tier. Doesn't appear on most paid 'best summer camp' lists because there's nothing to monetize — but that's why it's a hidden gem for budget-conscious or homeschool families (added 2026-04-26).

items.label: Maker Camp — Library or makerspace cohort makes solo at-home much better
items.detail: Maker Camp (makercamp.make.co) is free and self-serve, but kids who do it alone at home often plateau by week 3. Look for a local library, science museum, or makerspace among the 2,000+ registered Maker Camp host sites worldwide — the cohort element transforms engagement (added 2026-04-26).

items.label: BrainPOP — 30-day free trial requires CC; cancel before day 30 to avoid charge
items.detail: BrainPOP's 30-day free trial requires a credit card upfront and auto-converts to the $129/yr family plan if not cancelled before day 30. Set a calendar reminder. The Grades 3-8 + Jr (K-3) combo at $159/yr is only $30 more if you have multiple kids — usually worth the upgrade (added 2026-04-26).

items.label: AAUW Tech Trek — $50 covers a $1,000+ residential STEM week
items.detail: AAUW Tech Trek (rising 8th-grade girls) is fully sponsored by AAUW donations — families pay only a nominal $50 fee + transportation, when the actual program cost runs $1,000+. Branches often waive even the $50 for families in need. Path is teacher/counselor nomination, NOT direct application — talk to your kid's 7th-grade STEM teacher in winter.

sections.title: Regional summer camp windows (2026)

items.label: Seattle metro / Pacific Northwest
items.detail: Most camps run Jun 22 – Aug 28, 2026, Mon-Fri weekly. Week of Jun 29 - Jul 3 often runs 4-day (Mon-Thu) due to Jul 4 weekend. Some camps also run 4-day week of Jun 15 due to Juneteenth (Fri Jun 19).

items.label: Bay Area / SoCal
items.detail: Jun 15 – Aug 7, 2026. Schools out earlier than Pacific NW so summer programming starts/ends 1 week earlier. Examples: Lawrence Hall (Berkeley), CAMP at The Tech Interactive (San Jose), California Science Center (LA), Birch Aquarium (La Jolla) all run Jun 15 – Aug 7.

items.label: Chicago / Midwest
items.detail: Jun 29 – Aug 7, 2026 typical. Northwestern CTD (Evanston + Chicago South Loop) is the canonical anchor.

items.label: NYC
items.detail: Late June through late August. AMNH typical Jul 6 – Aug 21. Member registration February; general March-April.

items.label: Year-round / online programs
items.detail: No summer window — Khan, Beast Academy, Synthesis, Code.org, Mystery Science (free trial through Jun 30, 2026), Generation Genius, Khan, NASA STEM virtual, Nat Geo Kids. Treat sessionPattern as 'year-round-classes' and don't gate on summer dates.

items.label: Single-day / event-based
items.detail: Burke Museum (Dino Trackers Jul 13 confirmed; rest of program runs through summer). Apple Camp at Apple Stores Jul-Aug. UW Engineering Discovery Days is an annual 2-day spring event — not a summer program.

items.label: YMCA Camp Orkila (overnight, Orcas Island)
items.detail: Registration opens Feb 4, 2026 at 6 a.m. Sessions 7-28 days, grades 3-12. Sliding scale (Price A/B); $50 deposit; financial assistance. Fills in days — set a calendar reminder.

items.label: Pacific Science Center Camps for Curious Minds
items.detail: Member early reg Feb 2; general public Feb 9. Scholarship apps open Feb 6 (separate from regular registration — apply to BOTH). Pay due in full by May 1 or balance auto-charged. 100+ themed weekly camps PreK-8 across 6 metro locations + new Bothell, Kenmore, Salish Sea.

items.label: Museum of Flight ACE (Aerospace Camp Experience)
items.detail: Member early reg Feb 20 11am PT, general public Feb 21 10am PT. K-9th grade. By April many K-3 sessions are at capacity (waitlist mode). Campership Program offers $100/$200/$300 financial aid. Contact ACE@museumofflight.org.

items.label: Camp Galileo Bellevue (STEAM Day Camp)
items.detail: Currently enrolling for Summer 2026. Early-Bird ends Feb 28 ($50/wk savings); rolling registration after. Multi-week + multi-sibling discounts stack. 9am-3pm M-F, optional extended care 8-9am + 3-6pm. Up to 75% need-based aid available.

items.label: Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium (Tacoma)
items.detail: Member registration Mar 10 8am, general public Mar 12 8am. Combined zoo + aquarium campus camps for ages PreK-8. Pierce County resident scholarship pool for EBT/WIC/foster/kinship families.

items.label: Lawrence Hall of Science (UC Berkeley)
items.detail: Member registration opened late 2025; general public Jan 2, 2026 — earlier than most CA camps. 2-week sessions ($625-950/wk) instead of 1-week — better content depth but longer parent commit. Financial aid available.

items.label: California Science Center (LA Exposition Park)
items.detail: Member presale Feb 18-24, 2026; general enrollment after Feb 24. Mix-and-match morning + afternoon classes for full-day flexibility. Member: $225 half-day / $450 full-day. Extended care +$110-120/wk; member rate saves $10/wk.

sections.title: Pricing tiers for K-8 enrichment (2026 reference)

items.label: Free / fully-subsidized
items.detail: PSC scholarships (up to 100%, application opens Feb 6), SPS Expanded Learning, NSBE SEEK (3-week virtual), Black Girls CODE Summer Camp (most participants pay $0), CYC SF, LA's BEST, Audubon Junior Birder, Khan Academy, Code.org, Camp Wonderopolis (NCFL-funded). Many YMCAs use sliding scale 'Price A/Price B' self-selected by household income.

items.detail: Camp Invention $245-295 with promo codes (CIFUN25 by 3/31, CIFUN20 by 4/28). CodeWizardsHQ $200-300 1-week themed online. Camp CrunchLabs $329 for 12-week summer Build Box subscription (~$27/wk). Most municipal parks dept day camps $150-300/wk subsidized.

items.label: Mid ($400-600/wk)
items.detail: Destination Science $400. Camp Galileo Bellevue (varies, typical $500/wk). Camp Tech Revolution $500. Music Works NW $530. Birch Aquarium $250-600 range. Northwestern CTD half-day starts $395.

items.label: Premium ($600-1100/wk)
items.detail: Lawrence Hall $625-950/wk (2-week sessions). AMNH Discovery Squad $575-650. Exploratorium $675-750. Field Museum $425-575 (1-week). iD Tech UW Seattle from $1099/wk. Lavner UW from $799/wk.

items.label: Specialty / residential ($2000+)
items.detail: Earthwatch Family Expeditions $2000-3500/wk + airfare (need-based aid via Ignite Awards covers up to 100%). iD Tech Academy 2-week overnight $4999+. Interlochen Junior $3500-5500/2-wk (need-based aid covers 30-100% for ~40% of campers). NYLF Pathways residential $1500.

items.label: Single-day specialty
items.detail: Burke Museum $90-100/day ($90 members; +$30 optional aftercare). Many museum 'mini-camp' options $50-150/day. Apple Camp at Apple Stores 100% free 90-min sessions Jul-Aug.

items.label: Hidden cost-leverage patterns parents should know
items.detail: (1) Member early-access at major museums = the highest-leverage piece — membership often pays for itself just from earlier access to popular camps. (2) Multi-week + sibling discounts often stack with Early Bird. (3) Scholarship windows often close mid-May — apply early. (4) Free school-district summer enrichment is often the best-kept secret in any local market — check district website starting March. (5) Steve & Kate's Camp auto-refunds unused day passes after summer (Bay Area + LA only). (6) AAUW Tech Trek runs $50 fee for what's normally a $1000+ residential STEM week (rising 8th-grade girls; teacher nomination).

sections.title: Washington Spotlight — neighborhood-level intelligence

items.label: Seattle proper
items.detail: Top picks: Pacific Science Center (member Feb 2 / general Feb 9, pay-by-May-1), Burke Museum (single-day camps; Dino Trackers Jul 13 confirmed), Museum of Flight ACE (Feb 20-21 reg, Jun 22 – Aug 28, K-3 sessions at capacity by April), Woodland Park Zoo (10 sessions Jun 22 – Aug 28, $585/wk, scholarships up to 100% in 20% increments), Seattle Aquarium Marine Camp (Pier 59, 5-day weekly Jun 22 – Aug 28), Seattle Children's Theatre Drama School (Seattle Center campus, ages 3.5-18), Music Center NW (north Seattle; Music Together camp verified Jul 20-24 $295). FREE: SPS Expanded Learning (May 1 deadline, kids under 60th percentile in math/reading), Lakeside LEEP (May 1 deadline, current 5th+8th graders only, 4-week free incl. transportation). Seattle Parks dept day camps (Camp Long, Carkeek, Discovery, Magnuson) $20-50/day.

items.label: Eastside — Bellevue / Kirkland / Redmond / Sammamish
items.detail: Top picks: Camp Galileo Bellevue (currently enrolling, Early-Bird ended Feb 28; weeks of Jun 15 + Jun 29 are 4-day due to Juneteenth + Jul 4; up to 75% need-based aid), DigiPen Open World (Redmond, ages 5-9 / 10-12 / 13-18 STEAM tracks), Music Works Northwest (Bellevue, verified 3 sessions: ages 4-9 Jun 22-26 $530, ages 8-12 Jun 29-Jul 1 $330, ages 12-16 Jun 22-26 $530), KidsQuest Children's Museum (downtown Bellevue, weekly ages 4-10), PacSci's second location at Bellevue + new Bothell + Kenmore + Salish Sea Elementary (same Feb 2 / Feb 9 reg as main). Bellevue + Kirkland Parks dept run sliding-scale day camps. Eastside generally runs $100-200/wk more expensive than Seattle proper for equivalent quality but waitlists are shorter.

items.label: South Sound — Tacoma + Pierce County
items.detail: Top picks: Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium (member reg Mar 10 8am / general Mar 12 8am — popular weeks sold out by April; Pierce County resident scholarship pool for EBT/WIC/foster/kinship), Tacoma Metro Parks day camps. Generally cheaper than Seattle/Eastside; less waitlist pressure.

items.label: Islands — Vashon, Bainbridge, Orcas
items.detail: Top picks: Camp Sealth (Vashon, ACA-accredited overnight + day; 8 sessions late June – end August, 4-13 days; 'Camperships' need-based aid especially generous for first-time campers + foster/kinship/EBT/WIC families). IslandWood (Bainbridge, 255-acre learning center; full-day grades 1-8, half-day Pre-K + K; cancellation by Apr 3 for full refund less $100 fee, by Jun 5 for 50%). KiDiMu Kids Discovery Museum (Bainbridge, half-day 9-12 or 12-3, $350 / $325 member). YMCA Camp Orkila (Orcas Island, residential 7-28 days grades 3-12; registration opened Feb 4, 2026 at 6 a.m. — popular sessions sell in days; sliding scale Price A/B; $50 deposit).

items.label: Bellingham + North Sound
items.detail: Top pick: Whatcom Family YMCA (weekly day camps Pre-K through 10, multiple tracks: Minis Camp ages 3-5, Discovery Camp 1st-5th, Outdoor + others; sliding-scale Price A/B + financial assistance). Far less inventory than Seattle metro but good cost/value for local families.

items.label: Spokane + Eastern WA
items.detail: Limited inventory in our curated DB — local YMCA + parks-dept day camps are the anchor. Mt Spokane hiking + outdoor day camps via local nature centers. Drive to Coeur d'Alene ID for premium options.
